children: Solvar
has forecast $21 million in normalised NPAT for the 2027 financial year while targeting a substantial earnings recovery from FY28 onward under its Strategy 2030 growth plan.
The specialist lender expects new loan originations to rise approximately 25% in FY27, with upfront customer acquisition costs and technology investment weighing on near-term profitability.
Its group loan book reached a record $999.4m in the first quarter of FY27, up 12.3% from the corresponding period, following stronger lending across consumer and commercial operations.
The longer-term strategy targets a $2 billion loan book and approximately $50m in NPAT by 2030, supported by expanded lending products, automation and productivity improvements.
Lending Momentum Builds
Australian continuing operations recorded $163.9m in first-quarter originations, a 72.7% increase on the previous corresponding period, while the Australian loan portfolio reached $979.3m.
Money3 generated $91.2m in originations, up 31.9%, while AFS contributed $31.6m, up 31.7%, and the newer Bennji commercial lending business originated $41.2m.
Bennji’s commercial loan book exceeded $100m in October and commercial lending across the Australian portfolio reached $150m by the end of the September quarter.
Continuing operations delivered quarterly interest income of $48.6m, up 9%, although normalised NPAT declined 30.9% to $5m because origination expenses are recognised before the related loan income.
Near-Term Earnings Lag

“With the strong growth in lending volume, it’s important to highlight that there is a lag effect—origination, or client acquisition costs, are taken up front when the loan is written and revenue is recognised over the life of the loan, typically four years across the Group,” chair Stuart Robertson said.
“To say it more succinctly, writing business today creates earnings tomorrow.”
Solvar plans to invest approximately $10m during FY27 to replace underwriting software and strengthen automation, AI, and the customer experience.
It expects those changes to improve operating efficiency and contribute to a material profitability uplift from FY28, when it is targeting more than $30m in normalised NPAT.
The group expects interest income from continuing operations to grow at a double-digit rate in FY27, although stronger lending volumes will increase funding expenses.
Improved Credit Quality
At the end of the first quarter, approximately 85% of the continuing loan portfolio fell into the strong and good credit categories, an improvement on the preceding financial year.
Annualised net bad debts stood at 4.2%, but Solvar expects economic pressures to push losses towards the upper end of its existing 3.5% to 4.5% target range.
The group has total debt funding capacity of $1.3 billion and more than $500m in available headroom across its diversified funding arrangements.
Its New Zealand portfolio continued its planned runoff, falling to $20.1m as management redirected capital towards Australian lending opportunities.
Dividend Policy Unchanged
For the 2026 financial year, continuing Australian operations generated $22.5m in adjusted normalised NPAT on a $920.3m loan book and $470.7m in originations.
Solvar distributed 19.5 cents a share in fully franked dividends during FY26, including 7.5 cents in special dividends, for total distributions of $36.7m.
Management anticipates 14 to 15 cents a share in dividends during FY27, including a special dividend, and expects its broader dividend policy to remain unchanged.
The group is aiming for loan book growth exceeding 15% in FY27 before the planned digital investment and larger lending base contribute to stronger earnings in subsequent years.

title: Solvar Prioritises Sustained Lending Growth over Near-Term Profit
